elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months" / "six (6) months"), and the conditional preferred elements are not all satisfied — the opt-out window is sixty (60) days rather than thirty (30), and no Vendor renewal reminder exists — so the mutual-written-agreement default is not displaced.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Base Agreement renews "for periods of twelve (12) months"; Attachment 1 renews "for periods of six (6) months" — both ≤ 12 months and unchanged by the redline.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Both rendered clauses require "sixty (60) days written notice of its intent to terminate" — twice the 30-day preferred window. To reach preferred, the drafter would have to render "thirty (30) days written notice" in both paragraphs.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Neither rendered paragraph contains any Vendor (MSL) notification obligation ahead of renewal; no reminder mechanic was inserted and none exists elsewhere in the cited text. A sentence obliging MSL to notify IBM in writing at least 60 days before each renewal date would be required.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewals "shall continue for successive periods under the same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties," so no unilateral price uplift is permitted — any change requires mutual written agreement.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Both operative sentences now read "unless either Party gives sixty (60) days written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement," replacing the six-month (Base) and twelve-month (Attachment 1) windows; 60 days is exactly at the fallback ceiling.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply — renewal is expressly on "the same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties," so no unilateral uplift mechanic exists to cap; retained language is Customer-favourable and untouched.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: both notice windows are rendered at sixty (60) days, and the price-cap element is inapplicable because renewals continue on the same terms absent mutual written agreement, so the finding is position-complete at the fallback and correctly classified as a deviation from the original six-/twelve-month windows (both beyond the 90-day walk-away threshold).

Preferred level fails on three elements: the opt-out window is 60 days rather than 30, there is no Vendor 60-day renewal reminder, and consequently the mutual-written-agreement default is not displaced. If the drafter wants preferred, render "thirty (30) days written notice" in both paragraphs and add an express MSL obligation to notify IBM in writing at least sixty (60) days before each automatic renewal date.

Minimal: the only textual change in each paragraph is the numeric notice period ("six (6) months" → "sixty (60) days"; "twelve (12) months" → "sixty (60) days"). Renewal term lengths, the initial three-year term, the Section 5.0 cross-reference, and the favourable "same terms and conditions" sentence are all retained, and no survival tails, procedures, or extra requirements were added.

Preserves intent: the mutual "either Party" structure, termination cross-reference to Section 5.0, and the requirement of mutual written agreement to change renewal terms survive without contradiction; no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling. The parallel edit to Attachment 1 also cures the internal anomaly of a notice window longer than the six-month renewal period it governs.
